subject: science
skillName: Rock Layers and Fossils Show Change
intro: Rocks often form in flat layers, one on top of another, over very long periods of time. Because new layers form on top of older ones, the bottom layers are usually the oldest and the top layers are the youngest. Fossils are the preserved remains or traces of living things found in these layers. By studying the patterns in the layers and the fossils inside them, scientists find evidence of how a landscape changed over time. For example, finding fish fossils in rock layers of a dry area is evidence that the area was once underwater.

items.prompt: In a cliff, rock layers are stacked from bottom to top. Which layer is oldest, and how do you know?

steps: Rock layers form one on top of another over time.
New layers are added on top, so older layers end up on the bottom.
Therefore the bottom layer is the oldest.
solution.answer: The bottom layer is the oldest, because new layers form on top of older ones.

items.prompt: Scientists find fish fossils in rock layers in a dry desert. What does this suggest about the landscape long ago?

steps: Fish live in water, so fish fossils formed where there was water.
Finding them in a now-dry area is evidence the area used to have water.
So the landscape was once covered by water, such as a sea or lake.
solution.answer: The desert was once covered by water, because fish fossils show water was there long ago.

items.prompt: Why can patterns in rock layers act as evidence of change over time?

steps: Each layer formed at a different time, recording the conditions back then.
Changes in the layers and their fossils show how the environment was different in the past.
So the ordered layers are like a record of the landscape changing over time.
solution.answer: Because each layer records a different time, and changes in the layers and fossils show how the landscape changed.

items.prompt: Where are the youngest rock layers usually found?

steps: New layers form on top of older ones.
So the youngest layers are at the top.

items.prompt: A layer with tree fossils lies above a layer with ocean shell fossils. Explain what this pattern suggests about how the area changed.

steps: The shell layer is lower, so it is older and formed when the area was ocean.
The tree layer is higher, so it is younger and formed when the area was land with trees.
This pattern suggests the area changed from being underwater to being dry land over time.
solution.answer: The area was once ocean (older shell layer) and later became dry land with trees (younger layer), showing it changed over time.

items.prompt: How could matching rock layers and fossils in two far-apart cliffs give evidence about the past?

steps: If two cliffs have layers with the same patterns and fossils, those layers likely formed at the same time.
Matching fossils suggest the two areas had similar environments long ago.
So comparing the layers is evidence about how large areas looked and changed in the past.
solution.answer: Matching layers and fossils suggest the areas formed at the same time with similar past environments, giving evidence about the past.
